thesis: Advanced nuclear technology company developing the Integral Molten Salt Reactor (IMSR) — a Generation IV small modular reactor using Standard-Assay Low Enriched Uranium (SALEU) fuel that sidesteps the HALEU supply-chain bottleneck facing many rivals. First MSR to complete CNSC Vendor Design Review and to secure NRC engagement, with a May 2026 NRC Safety Evaluation Report approving its Postulated Initiating Events topical report further de-risking licensing. A ~$292M October 2025 Nasdaq/SPAC raise left the balance sheet with ~$280M cash and multi-year runway. New Texas A&M RELLIS site lease and a Riot Platforms data-center collaboration tie the IMSR to AI power demand, but the company remains pre-revenue with no revenue expected until ~2030 and a pending, unconfirmed TETRA pilot criticality milestone.

drivers: TETRA pilot reactor achieves criticality under the DOE fast-track program, proving the technology
Further NRC topical report approvals continue to de-risk the licensing pathway
Texas A&M RELLIS site characterization advances toward a first commercial deployment
Riot Platforms and other data-center collaborations convert into firm nuclear-power offtake
First Construction Permit application filed by 2028, keeping early-2030s commercialization on track

base_case.assumptions: Licensing progresses but on a longer timeline; TETRA criticality slips or comes with caveats; RELLIS site work advances steadily; strong ~$280M cash cushions burn without an imminent dilutive raise; first revenue remains a ~2030 event with modest fleet buildout thereafter.

risks: NRC raises unforeseen safety concerns with the molten salt design or licensing stalls
TETRA pilot reactor slips further or encounters technical issues
Competitors (NuScale, Oklo, Kairos, X-energy) capture the SMR market first
Multi-year pre-revenue burn forces dilutive capital raises before commercialization
First commercial plant delayed to 2040+ or cancelled

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings release — cash position and burn update
TETRA pilot reactor criticality under the DOE fast-track program — a targeted milestone with no public confirmation it has been achieved
Further NRC topical report approvals — building on the May 2026 Safety Evaluation Report to de-risk licensing
Texas A&M RELLIS site characterization — advancing the ~77-acre first commercial deployment site
First Construction Permit application — major regulatory milestone toward commercialization

key_risks: Pre-revenue with no meaningful revenue expected until ~2030
TETRA criticality is a pending, unconfirmed milestone — slippage would pressure sentiment
Regulatory execution risk — NRC has never licensed a non-water-cooled commercial reactor
Dilution risk from future capital raises despite the strong ~$280M cash position
First-of-a-kind technology and deployment execution risk
Stock down 80%+ from SPAC highs and near its 52-week low signals market skepticism
